w10_T4_001618: Priya keeps 6 identical coin jars on her shelf and always treats every jar exactly the same way. Each jar started with 195 cents in it, which is just under two dollars. On Monday she dropped 50 cents into each jar, and on Tuesday she dropped another 50 cents into each. She then took 55 cents out of each jar for bus fare, added 19 cents to each jar from change she found on the pavement, and finally took 52 cents out of each jar to buy gum. How many cents are in all 6 jars together now?
w10_T4_001619: The Riverside library received a delivery of 4 crates, each holding 169 books. The books were divided equally between the library's 2 branches, and the main branch put its whole share on a brand-new shelf. The main branch has 12 staff members who look after that shelf. Over the next month a donor added 77 books to the shelf, 40 books that had been on loan were returned to it, 161 books were lent out from it, and 32 newly bought books were placed on it. How many books are on the main branch's new shelf now?
w10_T4_001627: Marcus bought 2 stamp albums at an auction, and each album held 186 stamps. He sorted every stamp equally into 4 display boxes and decided to keep just 1 of the boxes for himself. His friend Elena has 34 fewer stamps than Marcus keeps in that 1 box, so Marcus's box is the bigger collection of the two. At a stamp fair the following weekend, Elena bought 28 more stamps. How many stamps does Elena have now?
w10_T4_001628: In a trivia tournament, Hana's team started the final day with 238 points on the scoreboard. In the morning quiz they earned 22 points, and in the lunchtime quiz they earned 31 more. A penalty for a late answer then cost them 218 points, and a second penalty cost them 35 points, which put Hana's team behind Leo's team for the first time all day. In the lightning round every point on Hana's team's scoreboard was worth 8 points, and after that a bonus question added 13 points. How many points did Hana's team have on the scoreboard at the end of the day?
w10_T4_001631: Oliver and Sophie were both raising money for the school raffle. Oliver collected 151 dollars on Friday and another 57 dollars on Saturday. Sophie, who is far more persuasive, collected twice as much over those two days as Oliver did in total. On Sunday Sophie collected 57 dollars more. The raffle will have 30 prizes altogether. Sophie then spent 416 dollars of her money buying the prizes and 17 dollars on wrapping paper. How many dollars does Sophie have left?
w10_T4_001635: Amir and Beatriz spent Saturday picking apples at their uncle's orchard. Amir picked 58 apples before breakfast, 44 more before lunch, and 30 in the afternoon, while Beatriz spent most of the day chatting with the 5 farm workers. Feeling generous, Amir gave half of his apples to Beatriz, so the two of them ended the day with equal amounts. Beatriz divided her apples equally into 3 crates and drove 1 crate to her grandmother, who already had 38 apples in her kitchen. How many apples does her grandmother have now?
w10_T4_001638: Early in the morning, the Casa Rosa food truck prepared 3 trays of tacos with 35 tacos on each tray. Late in the morning the cook made 69 more tacos, and at noon she made another 15. During the busy afternoon the truck sold 139 tacos. In the evening the cook made 24 more tacos for the late crowd. How many tacos did the truck have on hand at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_001641: Diego logs his cycling time in minutes rather than hours, even though his coach, one of a dozen coaches at the club, prefers to see hours. On Monday he set out to ride for 44 minutes, but a flat tyre made him stop 3 minutes short of that. On Tuesday he rode for 79 minutes, on Wednesday for 76 minutes, on Thursday for 78 minutes, and on Friday for another 78 minutes. Diego knows that sixty minutes make one hour, but he still wants his weekly total written in minutes. How many minutes did Diego ride in total that week?
w10_T4_001643: Early in the morning Nadia collected 69 eggs from the barn and 41 eggs from the henhouse. Her stall at the market is 9 kilometres from the farm. By mid-morning her neighbour Tom had delivered a batch of exactly the same size as everything she had collected so far, doubling her stock. She then found 3 more eggs behind the tractor. In the afternoon she collected 43 eggs from the far field and 11 from the young hens. In the evening she sold 27 eggs to the baker. How many eggs did Nadia have at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_001653: Kofi sat down at a card table with 32 chips. He lost 17 chips in the first hand and another 9 chips in the second, then won 56 chips in the third. In the wild-card hand his stack of chips quadrupled. Under the table's rules, a wild-card winner must then share his whole stack equally among the 4 players at the table, himself included, so Kofi kept only his own equal share. In the final hand, one of a dozen hands played that night, Kofi lost 36 chips. How many chips did Kofi have at the end?
w10_T4_001658: At the school fair, the price of a lemonade was set at 185 cents in the morning, and a 15-cent cup charge was added on top of that. In the afternoon the organisers cut the price by 137 cents to clear stock, and then knocked off another 15 cents. In the evening they announced a half-price deal, halving the price again. The fair had 320 visitors that day. Just before closing, Marta bought 5 lemonades at the evening price and paid in cents rather than dollars because the stall had no notes, remembering that one hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents did Marta pay in total?
w10_T4_001662: Ravi and Meera are racing each other through a stack of novels. On Monday Ravi read 74 pages, and Meera read only half as many pages as Ravi did that day, so Ravi was ahead. Meera then picked up her pace: she read 46 pages on Tuesday, 78 pages on Wednesday, 35 pages on Thursday, 63 pages on Friday, and 69 pages on Saturday. How many pages did Meera read in total from Monday to Saturday?
w10_T4_001669: Petra started the week with 12 dollars in her purse. Her friend Jonas had 6 dollars less than Petra, so Petra was the richer of the two. Jonas spent 2 dollars on a bus ticket and then earned 64 dollars washing cars over the weekend. His mother, who always pays him in dollars rather than cents because she says counting one hundred cents to the dollar takes too long, gave him 50 dollars for his birthday, and his grandfather gave him 80 dollars. How many dollars does Jonas have now?
w10_T4_001676: On Monday morning, courier Sam mapped out a new delivery route made of 6 stretches of 24 kilometres each. Later that morning the dispatcher added a 64-kilometre detour to a farm, and at noon a 56-kilometre extension to the port. In the afternoon Sam found a bridge that cut 160 kilometres off the route. In the evening he agreed to drive the finished route 8 times every week for the next 6 weeks. How many kilometres will Sam drive on this route over those 6 weeks?
w10_T4_001682: On Tuesday morning the Sunrise Bakery's first oven turned out 74 loaves, and a second batch from the same oven added 28 loaves. The bakery has 3 identical ovens, and each of the other ovens produced exactly the same morning total as the first. The bakery employs 9 people. In the afternoon the bakers made 13 rye loaves, 59 sourdough loaves, and 56 baguettes on top of the morning's output. In the evening the manager worked out that Tuesday's total was typical, and that the bakery would produce exactly the same total on each of the 7 days of the coming week. How many loaves will the bakery produce over those 7 days?
w10_T4_001686: Ines packed a jar of honey weighing 124 grams into a box, and the box and padding added 46 grams to the package. Her brother Luca's parcel of preserves weighed 5 times as much as Ines's whole package, so his was by far the heavier of the two. Every delivery day Luca ships a double order, meaning 2 parcels of that weight, and there are 4 delivery days each week. He kept that up for 3 weeks. Luca weighs everything in grams even though the courier charges by the kilogram, and he knows that one thousand grams make a kilogram. How many grams did Luca ship in total over those 3 weeks?
w10_T4_001687: On Monday morning Tomas had 49 kilograms of clay in his pottery studio, and the morning class used 16 kilograms of it. In the afternoon a supplier delivered 12 kilograms more. Tomas then divided all the clay he had equally among 3 shelves, one for each of his evening classes. The studio has 8 pottery wheels. In the evening only 2 of those classes actually ran, and each one used up its whole shelf of clay. Tomas records clay in kilograms rather than grams, reminding students that one thousand grams make a kilogram. How many kilograms of clay did the evening classes use?
w10_T4_001693: In the morning Zoe printed 14 flyers as a test and then 59 more, and stacked them all in one pile. She then printed a second pile exactly like it, so she had twice as many flyers as before. Zoe kept printing until she had 9 piles of that same doubled size in all, one for each of her 9 volunteers. In the afternoon one volunteer found 43 extra flyers in the van, and the team handed out 66 flyers at the station. In the evening the print shop, which is 4 streets away, dropped off 67 more flyers. How many flyers did Zoe's team have at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_001696: In the morning Ada sowed 9 rows of corn in her first field, putting 126 seeds in each row. She has 5 fields in total and sowed every one of them in exactly the same way that morning. In the afternoon she sowed 27 extra seeds in a corner patch while a dozen crows watched from the fence. Her tractor is 14 years old. In the evening she placed an order for next spring, asking for 4 times as many seeds as she had sown that whole day. How many seeds did Ada order?
w10_T4_001700: The Orion cinema has 216 seats in its main hall. For the festival week, 98 seats are permanently reserved for sponsors and 17 seats are out of order, so those cannot be sold. The cinema runs 8 screenings a day in the main hall, and the festival lasts 5 days. A dozen ushers work in the hall during the festival. How many seats in total can be sold to the public over the whole festival?
w10_T4_001701: Bea had 197 stickers in her album, which has 40 pages. She gave 185 of them to her classmates and then won 48 stickers at the school fair. She sorted all the stickers she had left into 3 equal packs. Her friend Carl, who has been collecting for a dozen years, has 9 times as many stickers as there are in one of Bea's packs, so Carl has far more than Bea. Carl then gave 79 stickers to his sister and bought 45 new ones. How many stickers does Carl have now?
w10_T4_001705: Ali arrived in town with 107 minutes to spare before his train. He spent 88 minutes in the museum and 3 minutes walking to the station. When he got there, the board showed his train delayed by 34 minutes, and a little later the delay grew by another 23 minutes. The board shows delays in minutes rather than hours, and Ali knows that sixty minutes make one hour. Counting from the moment he reached the station, how many minutes did Ali have to wait for his train?
w10_T4_001707: On Monday morning the farm's main pump was delivering 78 litres per hour into an empty reservoir, and after a filter change it delivered 63 litres per hour more. By late morning a second identical pump was running alongside it, doubling the flow. In the afternoon a small backup pump added 45 litres per hour on top. All the pumps then ran together at that combined rate for 6 hours a day for 6 days. On the evening of the last day the farmer drew 10349 litres out of the reservoir for irrigation; he measures water in litres rather than millilitres, since a thousand millilitres make a litre. How many litres were left in the reservoir?
w10_T4_001708: A factory machine stamps 236 bottle caps every minute, and the factory runs 4 identical machines side by side. Each production cycle lasts 7 minutes. Half of the caps from every cycle fail inspection and are melted down, and only the rest are packed. The factory runs 9 cycles per shift and 7 shifts per week, and the current contract runs for 7 weeks. The manager tracks output per minute but reports it per hour, reminding the crew that sixty minutes make an hour. How many caps will be packed over the whole contract?
